db_evidence.notes: The correct evidence exists only as raw 30sec episode captions at 63960-64020 (visible via SQL LIKE '%chariot%'/'%cart%'/'战车%' over the full episodes table, or a raw time-window scan of episodes 63700-64400) -- describing the character 'collapsing/dissolving into golden particles, screen fades to black' then a 'revival/respawn sequence [that] replays the same scene'. This fight was NOT chunked into any event_chains/event_steps row (query for event_chains 63000-65000 returns 0 rows) and NOT tagged as an entity containing 'chariot'/'战车'. The only entity row matching 'chariot'/'战车' in the whole DB is entities:000633 '赤金战车 (golden war chariot boss)' at 71970-72000s, which belongs to a completely different, later boss fight that the visual sub-agent (correctly, in all 4 failing rollouts) confirmed has 0 deaths. Semantic_search over entities/episodes/event_steps/topic_facts consistently ranked the mislabeled 71970-72240 window above the true 63960-64020 window for every 'brown/iron chariot' style query.

root_causes: Database indexing gap: the true target boss fight (63960-64020) was never given an entity record or event_chain/event_steps entry containing 'chariot', so entity-lookup and semantic_search paths (used by 4/5 rollouts) systematically missed it and converged on a differently-named but keyword-similar boss ('赤金战车 golden war chariot boss') at 71970-72240.

Only rollout 2 escaped the trap by running a broad, time-unrestricted SQL LIKE search over raw episode text for 'chariot'/'cart'/'战车' instead of relying solely on semantic_search/entities, which surfaced the correct interval that other rollouts never queried.

The visual sub-agent (clip_qa) was accurate in every rollout given the window it was pointed at -- it never misread deaths vs knockdowns; the failures are entirely a retrieval/localization problem, not a visual counting problem.

Rollout 3 did attempt an event_chains query spanning the correct time range but got 0 rows (because the fight isn't chunked into event_chains) and did not fall back to a raw episodes text scan of that range, so it also missed the true window.
what_worked: Rollout 2's broad, unbounded-time SQL LIKE search across the full episodes table for the entity keyword ('%chariot%' OR '%cart%' OR '战车%') found the correctly-worded caption text that semantic_search/entities missed.
Rollout 2 additionally sanity-checked the alternative (wrong) window with a second clip_qa call and confirmed 0 deaths there, ruling it out before committing to the answer.
clip_qa reliably distinguished true death/respawn (character dissolves, fades to black, respawns) from mere knockdown/stagger across all 5 rollouts when given the right window.
transferable_lessons: For entity-keyword questions ('the Brown Iron Chariot'), do not rely solely on the entities table / semantic_search — run a raw SQL LIKE text scan over the full, time-unrestricted episodes table for the keyword and its likely Chinese/English variants before narrowing to a time window, since an entity may exist in captions without ever being extracted into the entities or event_chains tables.

If an event_chains query over a plausible time window returns 0 rows, treat that as 'this fight wasn't chunked', not as 'this fight doesn't exist here' — fall back to raw episodes-text search in that same range rather than abandoning it.

When multiple boss fights share a similar name/theme (e.g. two different 'chariot' bosses), verify by visually checking BOTH candidate windows with clip_qa before submitting, as rollout 2 did, rather than accepting the first entity/semantic-search hit.

A single strongly-matching entity name is not proof of the right time window — cross-check its interval against the question's implied scene details (e.g. burning wooden chariot dissolving into particles) via the actual episode caption text.
